title: Handing over care while you are away
description: Give someone close access to the plants and instructions they need, see the actions taken and end the access once you are back.

blocks.text: Before leaving, the owner picks the plants, adds instructions of their own and gives the helper access to them. The helper sees the most recent actions and marks what has been done, and the owner does not have to sort it all out over messages.

quote.text: One suggestion I would make is that it needs to develop an ability for us to share schedules. It is quite odd if a household has more than one people taking care, and couldn’t see each others activity.

blocks.text: Hand clear care to someone close

To begin with, one collection, two participants and distinguishable “checked” and “done” marks are enough. Once you are back, the temporary access can be ended, keeping the events in the plants’ history.
End the handoff without losing the history

The review is about shared care at home; being away is a narrower hypothesis about the same mechanism. It is worth testing on a real handover of duties: are the instructions clear to a person who does not usually look after this collection.
